title: Terraform drift detector and automated repair flows for Private node health regressions
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Goal: Implement a safe, auditable Terraform drift detection and automated repair flow for common Private (VPC) node health regressions (probe timeouts, agent process crashes, certificate expirations, lost route table entries). The task will add a drift-detector service, a minimal reconciler that performs plan-only checks against the Terraform state, a verified apply path with locking and canary percentage, and a runbook for SREs that covers escalation and manual override. Scope excludes refactoring existing Terraform modules themselves except where small, well-reviewed fixes are required to make them idempotent.
background: We see recurrent incidents where Private nodes degrade (agent disconnects, kernel panics after upgrades, IAM/role drift) and the observable symptom is healthcheck failures from the private-control-plane. Current remediation is ad-hoc: manual terraform plan/apply or re-deploying VMs. This ticket standardizes detection and automates low-risk repairs while preserving operator control and audit trails.
out_of_scope: Large module rewrites, on-prem air-gapped deployment plumbing, automatic OS-level reimaging (this ticket will surface that as a remediation suggestion but not perform it).
success_metrics: 50% reduction in manual paging events for driftable infra issues within 6 weeks of rollout
Automated repairs execute with zero failed changes >95% of runs in staging
All automated applies are logged with a Terraform plan output stored in the audit S3/Dash board
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled drift-detector job runs every 15m against all private VPC states and records plan diffs to the drift index
When plan-only diff crosses configured thresholds (tagged resources changed, >3 resources affected, or networking changes), the reconciler enqueues a canary repair
Canary repairs run in staging first, then production only after a manual approval step from on-call or via a signed automation token
All reconciler actions produce an immutable audit entry with plan output, PR link if changes originate from infra repo, and operator who approved
Runbook documented and validated with a tabletop exercise (SRE + Infra) and linked in on-call rotation
implementation_notes: Backend: use existing S3 Terraform state + DynamoDB locktables; ensure IAM roles used by reconciler have only plan/apply permissions scoped to target state
Drift-detector: lambda/cron service that does 'terraform init && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -out=drift.plan' and stores human-readable plan in S3 with metadata (timestamp, state key)
Thresholds: use heuristics - network/security-group changes OR >3 resource diffs OR agent user-data changes => require manual approval; smaller diffs allow automated canary apply
Reconciler flow: staged apply -> smoke tests -> staggered production canary -> roll forward if green, rollback if smoke fails
State locking: always acquire DynamoDB lock and verify lock owner; abort if lock held >10m and alert on-call
Safety gates: plan validation via 'tflint' and 'terraform validate' before apply; dry-run apply with 'terraform apply -auto-approve drift.plan' only from reconciler service token
Audit: persist complete plan and apply outputs to S3 with KMS encryption; emit event to internal audit webhook and to Console observability with a link
Manual override: runbook shows commands to reproduce drift locally: 'terraform workspace select <ws> && terraform plan -out=local.plan' and steps to lock state manually
Quick checks: 'ssh <node> -- sudo systemctl status redwood-agent' and 'journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 300' (for on-call investigative steps), 'aws ec2 describe-instance-health' for ASG-backed nodes
Canary percentage: default 5% of nodes in affected ASG; configurable per-environment via config map in infra repo
Integration tests: add CI job 'infra/drift-reconciler:smoke' that applies a mock change in disposable staging and asserts reconciler can detect and repair
Notifications: reconciler posts to #private-infra-incidents with short plan summary and link to full plan; only posts automated-apply completion events when fully successful
runbook_snippets: Force-lock state (operator): aws dynamodb put-item --table-name tf-locks --item '{"LockID":{"S":"<state-key>"},"Owner":{"S":"<operator>"}}'
Manual local repro: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/private-infra.git && cd private-infra/envs/prod && terraform init && terraform plan -out=local.plan
Apply (reconciler automated): reconciler will run 'terraform apply -auto-approve drift.plan' under locked state; if apply fails it will call the rollback hook and notify on-call
Manual recovery (agent crash): ssh node && sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sleep 30 && sudo systemctl status redwood-agent
Escalation: if automated repair fails twice for same state within 24h, open incident: https://tracker.redwood/cases/new?source=drift
security_considerations: Reconciler uses a short-lived signed CI token stored in AWS Secrets Manager; token rotation enforced weekly
All apply events must be approved by a user with 'infra:approve' in IAM; reconciler can use a signed approval token generated via a 2-step web UI
Plan/Apply outputs stored in S3 must be encrypted with customer KMS keys for private deployments; ensure cross-account access boundaries
Audit log retention configured to 1 year for production states; older artifacts archived to Glacier
Do not embed secrets in terraform plans; reconcile service strips sensitive values from saved plan files
